rule.name: Privileged Container Enabled
rule.rule_desc: The code or deployment configuration requests privileges or grants access beyond an explicitly resolved minimum. Determine the effective permissions and the operation’s requirements.
rule.vuln_desc: A compromised actor may access additional data, modify protected resources, or extend compromise beyond the intended application boundary when excessive privileges remain available.
rule.developer: Run with the least privileges required, remove unnecessary grants, and scope each permission to its intended resource and operation. Verify effective inherited permissions and test denied access.
rule.reviewer: Privileged containers are a critical finding. Verify any exceptions are justified by a specific operational need (e.g., node-level DaemonSets). This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.vuln_desc: A compromised actor may access additional data, modify protected resources, or extend compromise beyond the intended application boundary when excessive privileges remain available.
rule.developer: Run with the least privileges required, remove unnecessary grants, and scope each permission to its intended resource and operation. Verify effective inherited permissions and test denied access.
rule.reviewer: Confirm allowPrivilegeEscalation is false or absent (default should be false in restricted PSA). This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.vuln_desc: A compromised actor may access additional data, modify protected resources, or extend compromise beyond the intended application boundary when excessive privileges remain available.
rule.developer: Run with the least privileges required, remove unnecessary grants, and scope each permission to its intended resource and operation. Verify effective inherited permissions and test denied access.

rule.name: Read-Only Root Filesystem Not Enforced
rule.rule_desc: The workload does not enforce a read-only root filesystem. Determine whether writing to image paths is necessary and which volumes remain writable.
rule.vuln_desc: A compromised workload may modify image files or configuration and retain unwanted changes within its writable layer; this can aid persistence but does not by itself grant host access.
rule.developer: Use a read-only root filesystem where compatible and mount only required writable directories. Restrict volume permissions and keep executable and configuration paths immutable.
rule.reviewer: Confirm containers use read-only root filesystems wherever possible. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Host PID Namespace Shared
rule.rule_desc: The workload shares the host process namespace.
rule.vuln_desc: A compromised container may observe host process information and, when additional permissions permit it, signal or interfere with host processes, expanding the impact beyond normal container isolation.
rule.developer: Disable host PID sharing unless a documented operational requirement needs it. Minimize process capabilities and restrict the workload to an appropriately isolated node.
rule.reviewer: Confirm hostPID usage is justified by a node-level operational requirement. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Host Network Namespace Shared
rule.rule_desc: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
rule.vuln_desc: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
rule.developer: Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.
rule.reviewer: Verify hostNetwork usage is limited to justified infrastructure components. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Host IPC Namespace Shared
rule.rule_desc: The workload shares the host inter-process communication namespace.
rule.vuln_desc: A process with the necessary permissions may access host IPC resources or shared-memory content, exposing data or interfering with host applications.
rule.developer: Disable host IPC sharing unless it is essential. Isolate required host-integrated workloads and restrict IPC resource permissions and process privileges.
rule.reviewer: Confirm hostIPC is restricted to justified low-level infrastructure workloads. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Secret Exposed as Environment Variable
rule.rule_desc: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
rule.vuln_desc: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
rule.developer: Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.
rule.reviewer: Verify secrets are mounted as volumes rather than environment variables where possible. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: No Resource Limits Defined
rule.rule_desc: The code configures failure handling or resource consumption. Determine whether failure paths preserve security invariants and whether work is bounded.
rule.vuln_desc: Unhandled failures or unbounded work may disrupt availability or leave security-relevant state inconsistent. The presence or absence of a named handler alone does not establish a reachable security defect.
rule.developer: Bound resource use, handle failures at the correct ownership boundary, and fail safely before updating trusted state. Test exceptional paths, cancellation, timeouts, and recovery behavior.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all containers have defined resource limits. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Default Service Account Token Auto-Mounted
rule.rule_desc: The workload may receive an automatically mounted Kubernetes service-account token.
rule.vuln_desc: A compromised process may use the token to call the cluster API with the service account’s granted permissions, extending access beyond the application’s intended resources.
rule.developer: Disable token automount when cluster API access is unnecessary. Otherwise use a dedicated, narrowly privileged service account and short-lived projected tokens.
rule.reviewer: Confirm automountServiceAccountToken is false for all workloads that do not explicitly require Kubernetes API access. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
